name: Do You Need a Permit for Roof Replacement in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Permit requirements in Los Angeles County depend on the city, the size of the project, and whether the work is a repair or a full re-roof. Small repairs are often treated differently from complete replacement. If the job includes structural changes, deck repairs, new underlayment systems, or ventilation upgrades, permitting is more likely to be required. Because Los Angeles County includes many cities with their own rules, the contractor should verify local requirements before demolition starts. Homeowners should ask who is pulling the permit, what inspections are expected, and whether permit fees are included in the proposal. A contractor who skips this step can create delays, failed inspections, or resale issues later. For a good bid comparison, make sure each estimate states whether permitting, plan review, and inspection coordination are included. That way you are comparing the same scope of work instead of guessing.
acceptedAnswer.description: A roof replacement often requires a permit, especially when the work involves structural changes, re-roofing limits, or code-related upgrades. Simple minor repairs may not need the same level of permitting. Requirements can vary by city and by the scope of work, so the contractor should confirm permit rules before starting.
